decisions: The webhook secret is timing-safe compared in Fastify onRequest before body parsing or any repository, owner-state, or Telegram call.
Only the configured numeric owner in the matching private chat is accepted; every unauthorized or non-private update receives the same generic Telegram refusal and an opaque HTTP acknowledgement.

A security-definer Postgres function atomically claims the unique update identity and captures the optional authenticated owner delivery chat; the persistence interface accepts no webhook payload or message text.
The controlled walking-skeleton responses are exactly 'No active promises.' for empty status and one bounded status-guidance line for other owner text; model and commitment behavior remain deferred.
A claimed update is never processed or sent twice, including concurrent replay; outbound Telegram is isolated behind an injectable server-only client.
deviations_from_plan: The QA sandbox denied approved disposable-database mutation and local Playwright port binding, so the lead context executed the immutable Node 24 commands while QA independently reproduced the webhook test and reviewed the results, migration, tests, state, and redaction scans; evidence records this split provenance.

One self-cleaning test attempt was abandoned and fully restored because cleanup would have required broadening intentionally narrow production table permissions; the disposable local database was reset from committed migrations after QA instead.
follow_ups: S01-03: replace the temporary unsupported-text guidance path with the bounded decision and draft flow while preserving the Telegram authorization, claim, and redaction seams.
S01-06: extend /status from the factual empty response to ordered active promises with versioned Done and Cancel actions.
S01-12: configure the deployed Telegram webhook and record a real owner/private, unauthorized, and replay-safe smoke without exposing identifiers or message text.

decisions: One declarative decision specification generates the strict API JSON schema, inferred TypeScript result type, and runtime structural validation without a new runtime dependency.

The OpenAI Responses adapter is stateless and tool-free, uses strict text-format schema output with store false, and enforces the configured server-only model, prompt version, credential, and five-second timeout.
Application semantic validation independently enforces the class/action/missing-field relationships, simple-action constraints, and future Asia/Singapore absolute targets.
Refusal, incomplete envelopes, HTTP and JSON failures, timeout, structural failure, and semantic failure map to bounded non-authorizing outcomes without raw provider material.
One benign synthetic live-provider request supplements exhaustive controlled tests; neither path writes product state or retains raw input, output, trace, or chain of thought.
deviations_from_plan: The original S01-03 exceeded the sizing rule and was split into S01-03a, S01-03b, and S01-03c, then S01-03a was narrowed to the provider contract; no acceptance criterion was weakened.
The QA sandbox denied the full repository gate's local test-server binding, so the lead context ran that immutable command while QA independently ran the exact engine suite and reviewed all evidence.

The single real-provider smoke ran at immutable commit 6697b6c before two review corrections; those corrections did not change its request or input, final controlled regressions cover the corrected handling, and no second provider request was made.
Two architecture correction cycles tightened completed-envelope, body-read timeout, and smoke-shape handling before the final PASS.
